transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-23
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Alan Chen (Summit Procurement), Priya Rao (Summit Legal), Diego Morales (Summit CTO), Sara Blake (Summit Security)
Recorded_at: 2026-02-23T16:00:00Z

Summary: quick commercial onboarding kickoff focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiering, egress pricing scenarios and residency constraints. Customer wants clear cost comparisons (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and to understand where data lives and KMS options; legal asked about liability caps, sub-processor lists, and audit rights.

Topics: MSA/DPA redlines, egress and networking fees, Dedicated capacity vs Hosted API, VPC/private deployment, KMS/HSM, SOC2 / audit artifacts, timeline to pilot, benchmark plan

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you taking time. Quick introductions, then we'll jump into the playbook.
[00:18] Alan (Procurement): Thanks Maya, Alan here — we'll be driving the vendor onboarding. Priya will handle legal, Diego for infra and momentum, Sara on security.
[00:32] Maya: Great, Jordan and I from Redwood. Jordan will cover the cost and technical contrasts.
[00:40] Jordan (SE): Hi all — quick heads up, I've got a spreadsheet we'll share that shows token-based costing and an egress line item.

[01:05] Priya (Legal): Hi quick Q — is the DPA you're planning to use the standard Redwood template or the enterprise variation? We got some comments around sub-processors and data deletion timelines.
[01:22] Maya: It's our enterprise DPA by default for customers with residency needs; we'll push a redline summary to you. For sub-processors, we maintain a published list but we can provide an auditable roster.

[02:10] Diego (CTO): For us residency matters — PHI-ish environment, so region locking and potential on-prem are in scope. We need clarity on private deployment options and SLA differences.
[02:28] Jordan: Right — we typically recommend three lanes: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated pools (committed GPU) and Private (VPC or on-prem). Each has different egress and operational costs.

[03:05] Sara (Security): On KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) and HSM-backed KMS? And is there key rotation visibility?
[03:22] Jordan: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. Hosted API can also integrate via a KMS proxy for enterprise. HSM-backed options are available in Private mode. Rotation logs are surfaced in the Console; we can share sample audit entries.

[04:00] Priya: Liability caps, indemnities — what's Redwood's approach? Our counsel usually wants a vendor cap tied to fees or a multiple.
[04:22] Maya: Standard MSA has a tiered cap; for enterprise we can discuss adjustments. Note that certain clauses like gross negligence remain carveouts. We'll surface the exact language in the redline.

[05:10] Alan: Egress is a concern — our finance team flagged potential surprise networking fees. We need examples of real customer egress billing.
[05:28] Jordan: Totally, egress is usually the trickiest. In hosted mode egress is a per-GB line in addition to token usage; for Dedicated, egress can be lower because routing is regional and we can compress/aggregate. Private on-prem has no egress to Redwood, but has operational overhead. I'll model 3 scenarios.

[06:05] Diego: For the Dedicated option, what's the SLA for latency and availability — and do you provide rollback/fallback to hosted if capacity?
[06:22] Jordan: Dedicated comes with an SLA for throughput and availability; we also offer automated fallback to a compatible hosted model in cross-regional outages. That fallback is configurable in the route policy.

[07:00] Priya: Audit rights — we need explicit audit clauses and a SOC2 report.
[07:15] Maya: We publish SOC2 Type II and can grant audit evidence/summaries. For additional audit rights we can include contractual language; we mark that as an exception in the DPA sometimes.

[08:10] Priya (interrupting): Also, data deletion: retention windows for logs, KV cache artifacts — how long do you keep logs by default?
[08:28] Jordan: By default logs retained 90 days in hosted; Dedicated and Private can adjust retention and we can push to customer's log collector. KV cache is ephemeral but debugging snapshots are retained per policy — we'll document that.

[09:05] Alan: Timeline — procurement needs a 30-day approval window once redlines are stable. We want pilot in Q2.
[09:20] Maya: Sounds doable — we can aim to have redlines back within a week and pricing models in 10 business days so you can get procurement review within 30 days.

[10:02] Diego: On cost modelling: besides token pricing and egress we care about quantization/throughput choices — e.g. cheaper quantized models might increase latency or affect quality.
[10:20] Jordan: Yep — in the spreadsheet I'll include quantized vs FP16 examples and expected speed/cost tradeoffs; we'll annotate quality impact.

[11:00] Sara: For private deployments — is networking peering needed? We want an architecture diagram and a list of required open ports and egress endpoints.
[11:18] Jordan: We'll share a network playbook: VPC peering options, NAT vs direct connect, ports, and a whitelisted endpoints list. We'll add a diagram for on-prem pack.

[12:05] Priya: Are you able to accept data residency commitments in contract (i.e., data stored only in eu-west-1)?
[12:20] Maya: Yes, we can contract residency for Hosted/Dedicated and Private naturally conforms. We will call out where backups or logs might transit — those are usually region-limited but will be explicitly stated.

[13:00] Alan: Pricing approvals — we need a single point estimate and an upper-bound scenario in case usage spikes.
[13:18] Jordan: I'll model a baseline, 2x spike, and 5x spike with egress skews; that'll give finance the upper-bound worst-case.

[14:05] Diego: Do you offer commitment discounts for Dedicated? We might commit to a monthly pool if pricing works.
[14:20] Maya: Yes, Dedicated is typically reserved commitment pricing with monthly/annual contracts. We can post the tiers in the pricing doc.

[15:05] Priya: One more legal — subprocessor notification windows, can you commit to notify within 30 days for any additions?
[15:18] Maya: Standard is publish-first with email notification for high-risk subs; we can agree to 30 days as an enterprise checkbox.

[16:00] Jordan: Quick tech note — latency profiles change by model and sequence length; our Console shows token-level latency and cost per route so you can see the economics in real time.
[16:30] Diego: Great, we want a demo of Console metrics in the security deep-dive.

[17:05] Alan: Ok logistics — procurement gate requires legal redline + a cost comparison + SOC2. If those are present, we can get to the final sign-off.
[17:25] Maya: Understood. We'll prioritize redlines and the cost comparison.

[18:10] Priya: Please include an explicit data flow diagram in the package — we need to show where PHI touches systems.
[18:28] Jordan: Will do, including tokenization and retention paths.

[19:00] Diego: For benchmarking, we want a short test plan: sample prompts, expected QA metrics, regen policy. Do you have a hosted sandbox for that?
[19:18] Jordan: We can provision a sandbox project with limited quotas for your team; we'll also provide a benchmark harness and test plan. Link will be attached.

[20:05] Sara: Regarding incident management — what's the P1 response SLA and how are notifications escalated?
[20:20] Maya: P1s are routed to 24/7 ops on enterprise contracts, with a 15-minute initial response target and follow-ups. We'll include escalation ladder in the SLA.

[21:10] Priya: Are there any non-standard DPA terms you typically push back on? For ex, data subject access process or right to audit frequency.
[21:30] Jordan: Audit frequency is negotiable; we push for reasonable timelines. DSAR handling is described in the DPA — we assist but customers retain the primary obligation.

[22:05] Alan: One finance ask — can you provide an amortized cost per 1M tokens including egress for us to model?
[22:20] Jordan: Yes I'll put that into the spreadsheet as '$ per 1M tokens' lines with egress per GB assumptions.

[23:00] Maya: Quick note on exceptions: We'll mark residency, audit rights, and cap adjustments as negotiable items; everything else stays standard.

[24:10] Priya: Also want to confirm data deletion proof — can you provide a certificate or machine-readable proof upon request?
[24:28] Jordan: We can provide deletion logs and an audit trail for deletion events; we typically don't issue a signed certificate but we can discuss SOW add-ons for that.

[25:00] Diego: On fallback routing, if Dedicated saturates, is traffic automatically queued or rerouted to hosted?
[25:18] Jordan: Configurable — you can choose fallback to hosted or queue; fallback usually preferred for availability but has cost/latency tradeoffs.

[26:05] Alan: Timeline recap — we need redlines, cost model, SOC2, and the benchmark plan to start procurement approval.
[26:20] Maya: We'll aim to deliver those artifacts within 7-10 business days.

[27:00] Priya: One procedural Q — does Redwood accept limited indemnity for data breaches tied to vendor negligence?
[27:20] Maya: We'll review, typically liability is capped but we can discuss carveouts for willful misconduct.

[28:10] Sara: Encryption at rest in transit — standard TLS? And stored model artifacts?
[28:22] Jordan: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest on customer keys where supported. Model artifacts for private deployments remain in-customer network.

[29:05] Alan: Are there examples of existing healthcare customers with similar egress patterns you can anonymize and share?
[29:20] Maya: We can share anonymized billing ranges and case studies. I'll ask Customer Success to pull a summary.

[30:00] Diego: Ok, final — please include a clear statement about where logs are stored and who has access.
[30:12] Jordan: We'll document access controls, RBAC, and log retention.

[31:05] Maya: Sounds like we have a plan. Jordan will do the cost model; I'll do the legal redline; we'll set up the security deep-dive.

[32:00] Priya: Quick clarification — for DPA deletion timelines, 30 days is tight for backups; can we do 90 days for certain backup artifacts?
[32:18] Maya: We'll call out which artifacts are subject to 90-day backup retention; primary data deletion can be 30 days with exceptions.

[33:00] Alan: Can the pilot be limited to EU region for residency testing?
[33:12] Jordan: Yes, we can spin up a region-limited sandbox and route everything to eu-west-1 for the pilot.

[34:05] Sara: Please confirm whether your telemetry includes raw prompt text in logs — if yes we need masking options.
[34:22] Jordan: Telemetry can be redacted; we also offer prefix/KV caching that removes PII from telemetry. We'll provide masking knobs.

[35:00] Maya: Action recap before we wrap.
[35:12] Maya: (1) MSA/DPA redlines — Maya to send summary and draft redline; (2) Cost model + egress scenarios — Jordan to send spreadsheet; (3) Security deep-dive scheduling — Maya + Sara to align; (4) Benchmark sandbox and test plan — Jordan to provision and share links; (5) Customer to send volumes - Diego.

[36:00] Diego: Confirming Diego will send volumes by March 1.

[37:00] Priya: I'll review redlines and flag non-negotiables.

[38:00] Alan: Procurement will wait for the cost model to start pricing approval.

[39:30] Jordan: I'll attach a short worked example showing egress at three volume tiers so finance can see sensitivity.

[41:00] Sara: For the security deep-dive, we want ops on the call. Could Redwood include a solutions architect?
[41:20] Maya: Yes we'll include a solutions architect and an infra lead.

[42:00] Maya: Anything else before we close?
[42:12] Priya: Please BCC procurement when you send redlines.
[42:20] Maya: Will do.

[43:10] Alan: Thanks everyone — this was productive.
[43:20] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the attachments.
[43:28] Maya: Meeting notes and next steps will be posted to the CRM.
